LESSON: WRITING 3.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: HANDWRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting, part of Strand 3 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How does being unable to read other people’s work make you feel? 2. Why should you ensure your written work is easy to read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use appropriate writing instruments (pencil first and then a pen) to copy a simple text,

2. print lower and upper case letters neatly and legibly,

3. pay attention to consistent letter size and height, direction of strokes such as dots, tails, crossbars, curves and differences in letter orientation like ‘d and ‘b,

4. write silent letters in words and phrases such as ‘please listen’ ‘I beg your pardon’, ‘may I borrow your watch’,

5. look up words and find the correct spelling from a digital device with peers,

6. consistently use the correct spelling of words with blends and double consonants. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use appropriate writing instruments (pencil first and then a pen) to copy a simple text,
2. print lower and upper case letters neatly and legibly,
3. pay attention to consistent letter size and height, direction of strokes such as dots, tails, crossbars, curves and differences in letter orientation like ‘d and ‘b,
4. write silent letters in words and phrases such as ‘please listen’ ‘I beg your pardon’, ‘may I borrow your watch’,
5. look up words and find the correct spelling from a digital device with peers,
6. consistently use the correct spelling of words with blends and double consonants. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner writes words legibly, neatly and spells them correctly.

• Learning to learn: This is developed as the learner builds on their writing skills by paying attention to consistent letter

size and height, direction of strokes such as dots, tails, crossbars, curves and differences in letter orientation.

Values:
● Love: It is shown as the learners work harmoniously with peers to look up words and find the correct spelling from a

digital device.

● Responsibility: It is enhanced as the learner uses the digital devices appropriately to look up words and find correct

spelling.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Self-esteem: This is developed as learner gains confidence in writing legibly and neatly.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of writing legibly and neatly in Kiswahili.
